qualification: Lexer-supported ASCII names, spacing, and escapes. This is a lexical disposition, not native-execution evidence for arbitrary source.
Typed name: Type = value declarations are mutable; native-verified example 002 increments its explicitly typed i32 count.
Explicit-width scalars and usize/isize. Integer addition, subtraction, and multiplication wrap; shift safety and other numeric edge cases remain incomplete.
Primitive casts require classification and range proof.
SPEC states evaluation order; no exhaustive side-effect-order qualification is claimed.
Native probes verify literal/range/capture matches and statement fallthrough; example suite covers labels and loops. Fall placement is restricted.
Direct and mutual recursion and known indirect cycles are rejected.
Declarations may parse but user variadic runtime lowering is rejected.
Multiple returns and destructuring are not backend features; use a result struct.
Use explicit receiver functions; dot-call methods are not current semantic support.
Native probes verify exactly sized nested/value array literals and zero initialization without an initializer. Scalar-fill initializers such as [3]i32 = 7 are rejected.
Native probe verifies same-shape [2]f64 addition. This does not establish tensor broadcasting or every numeric array shape.
Native probes verify half-open slicing, usize indexing, and slice .len. Full backing-storage lifetime enforcement remains incomplete.
new [N]T is rejected; use stack arrays or supported slice operations.
Tagged-union inspection is reserved and discriminant safety is incomplete.
Concrete function/struct examples exist; composite and call-chain propagation are incomplete.
Constraint syntax and semantic checks exist. A local @type_set alias passed semantics but failed Zig emission with unsupported TYPE_SET; native support is limited.
Ordinary lvalues pass to ref parameters; nil proof required for heap refs.
Direct use-after-del checks do not establish full alias or lifetime enforcement.
Automatic memory management is planned and not the current manual new/del model.
Simple alias calls lower to one combined Zig file; broad cross-module typing remains incomplete.
Resolver metadata is not runnable backend support.
Not a supported public executable import workflow.
No implemented public concurrency model.
Option, Result and collection modules are planned.
